common_distractors: a curve that crosses the equilibrium level
a curve that stops short of the edges of the rectangle
a curve drawn through the wrong point
a curve whose slope conflicts with the nearby segments
archetypes.description: A slope field for a given differential equation is printed and the response must draw the solution curve through a stated point.
difficulty_variables: whether an equilibrium level runs through the window
where the initial point sits relative to it
how far the curve must extend
expected_solution_path: locate the initial point in the field
follow the segments to the right and to the left
keep the curve on the correct side of the horizontal segments
extend to the edges of the rectangle
archetypes.invariant_structure: The field is supplied rather than built, the initial point is marked or stated, and the whole part is worth one point awarded on the geometry of the drawn curve.
archetypes.multipart_structure: The opening part of a multipart free response question, worth one point.
archetypes.name: Solution curve sketched on a supplied slope field
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point, awarded only when the curve passes through the stated point, extends reasonably close to the left and right edges of the given rectangle, has no obvious conflict with the drawn segments, and lies entirely on the correct side of the horizontal segments marking the equilibrium level. Only the portion inside the printed field is considered (sg-23:9, sg-24:9).
typical_wording: a portion of the slope field for the differential equation is shown; sketch the solution curve through the given point
wrong_approaches: solving the differential equation first and plotting the formula

common_distractors: evaluating the right side at the wrong lattice point
drawing all segments with the same tilt
matching on the visual density of the field rather than on the zero slope locus
common_givens: a differential equation or a printed field
archetypes.description: The response must produce the segments of a field at named points, or decide which of several equations produced a printed field.
difficulty_variables: whether the right side contains one variable or both
whether the zero slope locus is a line or a curve
how many candidate equations share a feature
expected_solution_path: find where the right side vanishes
evaluate the right side at two or three distinguishing points
compare with the printed field
archetypes.invariant_structure: The slope at a point comes from substituting the coordinates into the right side, and the pattern of the field is settled by which variables the right side contains.
archetypes.multipart_structure: A single multiple choice item, or a short free response part.
archetypes.name: Slope field matched to or built from a differential equation
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Scored in the same shape as the printed field part: the drawing is accepted when the segments agree with the computed slopes, including the horizontal ones (sg-23:9).
typical_wording: sketch the slope field for the given differential equation at the indicated points
which of the following differential equations could have produced the slope field shown
wrong_approaches: solving the equation and differentiating the solution

common_distractors: antidifferentiating only one side
omitting the constant of integration
adding the constant after the exponentiation instead of before
keeping both branches of an absolute value when the initial condition settles one
common_givens: sometimes a stated bound on the quantity
archetypes.description: A separable differential equation and an initial condition are given and the response must produce the particular solution explicitly.
difficulty_variables: whether the dependent side antidifferentiates to a logarithm or a power
whether an absolute value must be resolved
whether the independent side needs a substitution
whether the answer must be explicit
expected_solution_path: separate the variables with a differential on each side
antidifferentiate both sides
include one constant
substitute the initial condition and solve for the constant
solve for the dependent variable
archetypes.invariant_structure: The right side factors, both sides are antidifferentiated, one constant is carried, the initial condition fixes it, and the answer is solved for the dependent variable.
archetypes.multipart_structure: The closing part of a multipart free response question, worth four or five points.
archetypes.name: Particular solution by separation of variables
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Four points in 2023: separating the variables, finding the antiderivatives, including the constant of integration and using the initial condition, and solving for the dependent variable. A response with no separation earns none of the four; a response with no constant earns at most the first two; the third point requires the first two and the fourth requires the first three; an antiderivative written without absolute value symbols stays eligible for all four (sg-23:12). Five points in 2024, with the two antiderivatives scored separately (sg-24:11).
typical_wording: use separation of variables to find an expression for the particular solution to the differential equation with the given initial condition
wrong_approaches: treating the equation as though the dependent variable were a constant

common_distractors: restarting the second step from the initial point
using the whole interval as the step size
evaluating the derivative at the target input
reporting a value with no visible steps
archetypes.description: A differential equation and an initial point are given and the response must approximate the solution at a stated input using a named number of equal steps.
difficulty_variables: whether the derivative expression depends on both variables
whether the derivative expression is imported from an earlier part
how many steps are asked for
whether a direction of error is also demanded
expected_solution_path: compute the step size
evaluate the derivative at the initial point and advance
evaluate the derivative at the new point and advance again
report the approximation with the steps shown
archetypes.invariant_structure: The step size is the interval divided by the number of steps, the derivative is evaluated afresh at each new approximation, and the work must be visible as expressions or as a labelled table.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart free response question, worth two points.
archetypes.name: Euler's method over two steps of equal size
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Two points: one for the demonstration and one for the answer with supporting work. The 2024 guideline required two demonstrated steps with the correct derivative expression and at most one error, and withheld the answer point when there was an error, while requiring an incorrect first approximation to be imported into the second step. The 2025 guideline required only the first step, with the correct initial condition, step size, and derivative expression, and discounted later simplification or rounding errors for that point. Both accept a labelled table, and both allow an incorrect value imported from an earlier part to earn the answer point with a consistent result (sg-24:17, sg-25:23).
typical_wording: use Euler's method, starting at the given input with two steps of equal size, to approximate the value of the solution at the stated input; show the computations that lead to the answer
wrong_approaches: solving the differential equation and evaluating the solution

common_distractors: arguing from whether the solution is increasing or decreasing
evaluating the second derivative at one point only
leaving the second derivative in terms of the first derivative
stating the direction with no reason
common_givens: sometimes a stated range for the quantity
archetypes.description: A tangent line or Euler approximation to a solution has been produced and the response must say whether it is an overestimate or an underestimate, with a reason.
difficulty_variables: whether the sign of the second derivative can be settled from a stated bound
whether the expression must be reduced to the dependent variable alone
whether the approximation is a tangent line or an Euler step
expected_solution_path: differentiate the right side with respect to the independent variable
substitute the equation to remove the first derivative
determine the sign over the interval
state the direction with that reason
archetypes.invariant_structure: The second derivative is produced by differentiating the right side of the differential equation, the sign of that expression is settled over the whole interval rather than at one point, and the direction of the error follows from the concavity.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart free response question, worth two points.
archetypes.name: Direction of an approximation decided from the second derivative of a solution
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the second derivative expressed in terms of the dependent variable, one for the direction with the reason. An expression left in terms of the first derivative does not earn the first point but stays eligible for the second. The reason must state that the second derivative is negative, or that the first derivative is decreasing, or that the graph is concave down, and must reach the conclusion; an argument resting on the second derivative at a single point does not earn the point (sg-23:11).
typical_wording: is the approximation an overestimate or an underestimate of the value of the solution, and give a reason for the answer
wrong_approaches: solving the equation and comparing numerically

common_distractors: writing an equality with no constant of proportionality
writing an equation for the quantity rather than its rate
reversing the difference in a rate proportional to a gap
folding the initial condition into the equation
common_givens: a verbal description of a rate
a value of the quantity at a stated input
archetypes.description: A situation is described in words and the response must write the differential equation and identify the initial condition.
difficulty_variables: whether the rate is proportional to the quantity or to a difference
whether the independent variable is time
whether an initial condition is also demanded
expected_solution_path: name the dependent and independent variables
translate the proportionality into a constant multiple
write the derivative equal to that expression
record the initial condition separately
archetypes.invariant_structure: A proportionality word supplies a constant multiple, the derivative is of the modelled quantity with respect to the stated independent variable, and the initial condition is a separate statement.
archetypes.multipart_structure: A single multiple choice item, or the opening of a multipart free response question.
archetypes.name: Differential equation written from a verbal rate statement
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Scored as the setup stage of the separable question family: the equation must carry a constant of proportionality and the correct derivative, and the initial condition is used later to fix the constant of integration (sg-23:12).
typical_wording: write a differential equation that models the described rate of change, and state the initial condition
wrong_approaches: writing an exponential formula instead of the equation

common_distractors: checking only the initial condition
checking only that the shapes look alike
substituting the function but not its derivative
archetypes.description: A candidate function is offered and the response must decide whether it satisfies the equation, and sometimes the initial condition too.
difficulty_variables: whether the candidate carries an arbitrary constant
whether an initial condition must also be checked
whether the candidate fails only on part of the domain
expected_solution_path: differentiate the candidate
substitute the candidate and its derivative into both sides
compare
state the verdict and check any initial condition
archetypes.invariant_structure: The check is a differentiation followed by a substitution into both sides, and a single disagreeing input settles a negative answer.
archetypes.multipart_structure: A single multiple choice item, or a short free response part.
archetypes.name: Verification that a function solves a differential equation
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Scored as a demonstration: the derivative and the substitution must both be visible, and the conclusion must be stated. Scored here by analogy with the justification standards of the separable family (sg-23:12).
typical_wording: show that the given function is a solution to the differential equation
which of the following functions is a solution to the given differential equation
wrong_approaches: solving the equation from scratch when a verification was asked for

common_distractors: writing a linear model for proportional growth
omitting the constant of proportionality
reading the constant off a single data pair
reporting a number with no units
archetypes.description: A quantity whose rate of change is proportional to itself is modelled, solved, and read back into the situation.
difficulty_variables: whether the constant is positive or negative
whether a second data pair is supplied or must be read from a table
whether an interpretation is demanded
expected_solution_path: write the proportional model
separate and solve
use the initial value
use a second pair to find the constant
interpret with units
archetypes.invariant_structure: The equation is the constant multiple form, the solution is the initial value multiplied by an exponential, and one further data pair determines the constant.
archetypes.multipart_structure: A multipart free response question, or a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Exponential growth or decay model solved and interpreted
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Scored as the separable family with the exponential form as the target: separation, antiderivatives, constant with the initial condition, and the explicit solution (sg-23:12), with a further point for an interpretation naming the quantity, the units, and the input (sg-23:2).
typical_wording: the rate of change of the quantity is proportional to the quantity; find an expression for the quantity at time t and state what the constant means in context
wrong_approaches: treating the constant of proportionality and the constant of integration as the same object

common_distractors: reporting the carrying capacity as the fastest change value
reporting the initial value as the limit
solving the equation before answering
using the wrong zero of the right side
common_givens: an initial value strictly between zero and the carrying capacity
archetypes.description: A logistic differential equation and an initial condition are given and the response must state the carrying capacity, the limiting value, and the quantity at which the change is fastest.
difficulty_variables: whether the equation is written with the carrying capacity factored out
whether the initial value is above or below the carrying capacity
whether an interpretation with units is demanded
expected_solution_path: read the zeros of the right side
name the nonzero one as the carrying capacity
use the sign of the right side and the initial value to state the limit
maximise the quadratic right side to get half the carrying capacity
archetypes.invariant_structure: Every answer comes from the equation and the initial condition alone; the equation is never solved, and the right side is a quadratic in the dependent variable with zeros at zero and at the carrying capacity.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One or two parts of a multipart free response question, or a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Logistic model interpreted without solving
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Scored as reasoning from the equation: a point for the value and a point for the reason drawn from the equation rather than from a solved formula, in the shape the CED prescribes for interpreting the model without solving (ced:145). A response that solves the equation and then reports the limit answers a harder question than the one asked and risks the reason point in the way the Chief Reader records describe (BC-ERR-99035).
typical_wording: the quantity is modelled by the given logistic differential equation with the given initial value; find the limit of the quantity as the independent variable grows without bound, and the value of the quantity when it is changing fastest
wrong_approaches: separating the logistic equation with partial fractions when only the limit was asked for

common_distractors: setting the quantity rather than its derivative equal to zero
ignoring the supplied bound that removes one factor
classifying with no sign statement
common_givens: a stated bound on the quantity
a range for the independent variable
archetypes.description: Without solving, the response must locate a critical point of a solution, classify it, or describe where the solution rises and falls.
difficulty_variables: whether a supplied bound is needed to isolate a factor
whether the classification is by sign change or by second derivative
how many critical inputs lie in the range
expected_solution_path: set the right side equal to zero
use the supplied bound to reduce the equation
solve for the input inside the range
argue the sign of the right side on each side
archetypes.invariant_structure: The derivative is handed over by the equation, a supplied sign fact isolates the factor that can vanish, and the classification rests on the sign of the right side on each side of the critical input.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart free response question, worth three points.
archetypes.name: Behaviour of a solution obtained from the differential equation itself
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Three points: considering the sign of the derivative, identifying the input, and the answer with justification. A second derivative evaluation at the input is accepted as an alternate justification (sg-24:10).
typical_wording: for the stated range, find the input at which the modelled quantity has a critical point and determine whether it is the location of a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither

asked_to_produce: the interval of validity, or the accumulation form
common_distractors: keeping both branches of an absolute value
reporting an interval that does not contain the initial input
claiming the formula holds for every input
leaving the answer implicit
archetypes.description: The response must produce a particular solution and say on what interval it holds, or write it as the initial value plus an integral.
difficulty_variables: whether the solution expression has a vertical asymptote
whether an absolute value must be resolved
whether the accumulation form is acceptable
expected_solution_path: produce the general solution
use the initial condition to fix the constant and the branch
identify where the expression fails to be defined
report the interval containing the initial input
archetypes.invariant_structure: The initial point lies in the interior of the interval of validity, the branch and the sign are settled by the initial condition, and the accumulation form is available whenever the right side involves only the independent variable.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart free response question, or a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Particular solution with a domain restriction or an accumulation form
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Scored as the separable family, with the branch choice folded into the constant point and the domain statement scored as part of the final answer where it is demanded (sg-23:12, sg-24:11).
typical_wording: find the particular solution to the differential equation with the given initial condition, and state the interval on which the solution is valid
wrong_approaches: choosing the branch by the sign of the constant rather than by the initial condition

variants.description: A row of horizontal segments marks a level the solution curve may not cross, and the sketch point turns on staying below or above it.
variants.name: Equilibrium level inside the printed window

variants.description: The curve only has to follow the segments and reach both edges of the rectangle.
variants.name: Field with no equilibrium level in view

variants.description: The curve must be extended further in one direction than the other to reach both edges.
variants.name: Initial point away from the centre of the window

variants.description: The field repeats along every row or every column, which makes the match decidable from one line of the grid.
variants.name: Right side depending on one variable only

variants.description: The slope varies in both directions, so several lattice points must be tested.
variants.name: Right side depending on both variables

variants.description: Two candidate equations vanish on the same set, so the match must be decided by the steepness away from it.
variants.name: Candidates sharing a zero slope locus

variants.description: The separated dependent side is a reciprocal, so an absolute value appears and must be resolved from the initial condition.
variants.name: Dependent side antidifferentiating to a logarithm

variants.description: The independent side is a composite such as a cosine of a linear expression, so the antiderivative needs a substitution.
variants.name: Independent side needing a substitution

variants.description: The rubric awards each antiderivative its own point instead of combining them.
variants.name: Five point split with the antiderivatives scored separately

variants.description: Each step needs a fresh evaluation in two arguments rather than one.
variants.name: Derivative expression depending on both variables

variants.description: The slope used in the first step is a value computed earlier in the same question, and an incorrect import stays eligible for the answer point.
variants.name: Derivative expression imported from an earlier part

variants.description: The steps appear as rows with named columns; in the presence of a correct answer the labels are not needed, and without one they are.
variants.name: Work presented as a labelled table

variants.description: Differentiating the right side leaves a first derivative that the equation itself replaces, which the rubric requires before the first point is earned.
variants.name: Second derivative reducible using the equation

variants.description: The question supplies a bound that fixes the sign of the second derivative across the whole interval.
variants.name: Sign settled by a stated bound on the quantity

variants.description: The approximation being judged is a multi-step Euler value, so the concavity must hold over the whole interval.
variants.name: Direction demanded for an Euler approximation rather than a tangent line

variants.description: The translation is a single constant multiple and leads to the exponential model.
variants.name: Rate proportional to the quantity itself

variants.description: The translation carries a subtraction whose order settles the sign of the approach.
variants.name: Rate proportional to a difference from a fixed level

variants.description: The part asks for both the equation and the value at a stated input, scored together.
variants.name: Initial condition demanded alongside the equation

variants.description: The response must show the candidate works rather than choose among several.
variants.name: Single candidate to be verified

variants.description: The family must be verified for every value of the constant, which is the content of the infinitely many solutions statement.
variants.name: Candidate carrying an arbitrary constant

variants.description: The function solves the equation but misses the stated point, so the verdict turns on the second check.
variants.name: Candidate that fails the initial condition only

variants.description: The rate constant is given, so only the initial value has to be used.
variants.name: Constant supplied in the statement

variants.description: A later value of the quantity is supplied and the constant follows through a logarithm.
variants.name: Constant recovered from a second data pair

variants.description: The quantity falls, and the interpretation must say so rather than reporting the size of the constant alone.
variants.name: Decay context with a negative constant

variants.description: The right side appears as a constant times the quantity times the difference from the capacity, so the capacity is visible directly.
variants.name: Equation written with the carrying capacity as a factor

variants.description: The right side is expanded, so the capacity must be recovered by factoring the quadratic.
variants.name: Equation written in expanded quadratic form

variants.description: The quantity decreases toward the capacity, so the sign argument runs the other way and the fastest change value is not attained.
variants.name: Initial value above the carrying capacity

variants.description: A stated inequality on the quantity makes one factor of the right side nonzero, so only the other can vanish.
variants.name: Supplied bound removing one factor

variants.description: The justification is a sign change argument on the right side of the equation.
variants.name: Classification by the sign of the derivative on each side

variants.description: The justification differentiates the right side and evaluates it at the critical input, which the rubric accepts as an alternate route.
variants.name: Classification by an evaluated second derivative

variants.description: The solution expression has a vertical asymptote, and the interval reported must be the one containing the initial input.
variants.name: Domain restriction created by a vanishing denominator

variants.description: An absolute value or a square root leaves two branches and the initial condition selects one.
variants.name: Branch settled by the sign at the initial point

variants.description: The right side involves only the independent variable, so the initial value plus a definite integral is a complete particular solution.
variants.name: Accumulation form accepted as the answer
